last_material_result: KILL — the bounded substitute/distribution check materially weakened Apartment Common-Fee Spike Explainer. Danjipyo already publishes K-apt-derived regional pages with explicit month-over-month rising/falling apartment rankings and monthly trend comparison, while gwanribi.kr exposes 22,000+ complexes with 17 fee categories and regional/complex comparison. Apartment-i already provides logged-in household line-item analysis and same-complex/same-size comparison. This leaves only the proposed causal 'why did it rise?' layer. But reliable causal attribution from public common-fee data alone is weak: generic explanations such as labor, energy, repair or reserve changes are easy content substitutes, while defensible complex-specific attribution would require joining and interpreting maintenance/procurement events with uncertain causality and higher maintenance burden. The apartment-name + management-fee SEO surface is also already occupied by public-data comparison sites. The remaining differentiation is therefore too thin relative to acquisition and explanation-quality risk.
economics: KRW0 spent. The candidate is killed before build. Hosting/data could have remained free, but expected marginal contribution is now judged too low because the indexable comparison surface is already commoditized and the only differentiated causal layer carries materially higher data-joining/quality burden. No sunk-cost reason to continue.
next_checkpoint: Next run: fresh genetic discovery for a standalone consumer data/content/alert product. Prefer a public-data transformation where the action layer is mechanically derivable rather than interpretive, and where incumbents expose raw data but not the consumer-facing decision/alert.
recommendation: KILL Apartment Common-Fee Spike Explainer and return to DISCOVER. Do not mutate into generic fee comparison, household bill analysis or manually researched causal explanations.
